# Computational evidence — Exp 569 / paper 216 (band-9 `x² − N` smoothness drift)

All numbers below were produced by short exploratory scripts (Python, seed `20260824`).
They are **exploratory**, not verified: every claim that this project asserts as
established is proved in Lean in `Catalog/Probability/U9Drift*.lean` and is marked as such.
The arithmetic of the reported intervals (coverage, deliverables, pooling, cluster
thresholds) is *entirely* re-derived inside Lean with exact rational arithmetic, so those
figures are verified rather than merely computed.

## 1. Arithmetic of the reported intervals (all re-proved in Lean)

| quantity | value | Lean theorem |
|---|---|---|
| pilot `1e6` CI | `[0.8630, 1.0389]`, centre `0.95095`, half width `0.08795` | `pilot1e6_center_eq`, `pilot1e6_halfWidth_eq` |
| replication `1e6` CI | `[0.919, 1.0101]`, centre `0.96455`, half width `0.04555` | `rep1e6_center_eq`, `rep1e6_halfWidth_eq` |
| pilot deliverable `max|edge−1|` | `0.1370` | `pilot1e6_edge` |
| replication deliverable | `0.0810` | `rep1e6_edge` |
| inverse-variance pooled point | `≈ 0.96167` | `joint_interval_upper_edge_lt` |
| inverse-variance pooled half width | `≈ 0.040447` | `joint_interval_upper_edge_lt` |
| pooled upper edge | `≈ 1.00212` (covers 1) | `joint_interval_covers_one` |
| candidate rate bracket (primary cut) | `[2.65701, 3.56128]·10⁻⁵` | `candidate_rate_pinned` |
| cluster threshold for a 1 % resolution | `2656` clusters (`20.75×` of 128) | `exact_cluster_threshold` |

Two adversarial catches came out of this re-derivation and are themselves theorems:

* the quoted candidate-rate bracket `[2.66, 3.56]·10⁻⁵` is rounded **inwards** and therefore
  is not an enclosure (`ledger_bracket_is_not_an_enclosure`); the outward-rounded
  `[2.65, 3.57]·10⁻⁵` is (`candidate_rate_safe_bracket`);
* the quoted joint point `≈ 0.97` is the **equal-weight** average of the two point
  estimates; inverse-variance weighting gives `≈ 0.981`, strictly closer to the null
  (`equal_weight_pooling_overstates_the_drift`), and the "√2-tightened" phrase does not
  apply because the two runs are not precision-matched
  (`sqrt_two_tightening_fails`).

## 2. Local density of `p | j² − N` (small cases)

For each odd prime `p` and random `N`, the number of residues `j mod p` with `p | j² − N`
was counted directly and compared with `1 + legendreSym(N, p)`:

```
p=    3 N mod p=    2 roots=0 1+chi=0
p=    3 N mod p=    0 roots=1 1+chi=1
p=    5 N mod p=    2 roots=0 1+chi=0
p=    5 N mod p=    1 roots=2 1+chi=2
p=    7 N mod p=    6 roots=0 1+chi=0
p=   11 N mod p=    9 roots=2 1+chi=2
p=   13 N mod p=    3 roots=2 1+chi=2
p=  101 N mod p=   31 roots=2 1+chi=2
p=  101 N mod p=   98 roots=0 1+chi=0
p= 1009 N mod p=  402 roots=2 1+chi=2
```

Agreement is exact in every case, as the Lean theorem `U9Drift.sqrtCount_eq` requires.

## 3. The multiplicative bias `∏_{p≤P}(1 + χ_p(N))`

Sampling `20000` random `N < 10¹²` and forming the product over the first `k` odd primes:

| k | empirical mean (theory 1) | empirical 2nd moment | theory `2^k` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 1.006 | 20.7 | 32 |
| 10 | 1.204 | 814.7 | 1024 |
| 15 | 0.410 | 3355.4 | 32768 |

The mean is close to `1` for small `k` and becomes *wildly unstable* by `k = 15` — with
20 000 draws the sample mean of a quantity with variance `2^15 − 1` is essentially
uninformative. This is precisely the content of `U9Drift.mean_signProd`,
`U9Drift.second_moment_signProd` and `U9Drift.variance_signProd`, and it is the reason a
smoothness-ratio study must resample whole `N`-clusters rather than pairs.

## 4. A miniature replication of the design (8 clusters, 48-bit `N`, `B = 5000`)

| N | candidate smooth | control smooth | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 229871916547937 | 34 | 24 | 1.41 |
| 200807072042177 | 31 | 25 | 1.24 |
| 271077539025707 | 11 | 21 | 0.54 |
| 171670900995397 | 29 | 23 | 1.26 |
| 177569514804709 | 43 | 31 | 1.38 |
| 222373491782989 | 34 | 22 | 1.53 |
| 211186360025533 | 32 | 28 | 1.14 |
| 217876760921539 | 31 | 29 | 1.07 |

Pooled ratio `1.21`; per-`N` ratios span `[0.53, 1.53]` on only `6000` draws per cluster.
Two exploratory observations (not verified claims):

* the **between-cluster spread is far larger than the within-cluster Poisson noise**, in
  line with §3 — this is the empirical signature that the effective sample size is the
  cluster count;
* at this very small `u` the candidate pool is, if anything, *more* smooth than the
  control, i.e. the sign of any deviation at small `u` is opposite to the sub-1 drift
  reported at band 9. No conclusion is drawn from eight clusters; it is recorded only as a
  motivation for the direction-of-drift conjecture in `FUTURE_DIRECTIONS.md`.

## 5. Sign-test check

Enumerating all `2^k` split-half sign patterns, exactly two are constant for every
`k ≥ 1`, so the direction-stability p-value is `2^{1-k}`: `0.25, 0.125, 0.0625, 0.03125`
for `k = 3, 4, 5, 6`. Hence four agreeing split-halves cannot reach the 5 % level; six can.
This is proved in Lean (`U9Drift.card_allSame`,
`U9Drift.split_halves_needed_for_significance`), so the table is a redundancy check rather
than evidence.

# Future directions — band-9 `x² − N` smoothness, after the round-74 replication

The formal results of this cycle live in `Catalog/Probability/U9DriftIntervals.lean`,
`U9DriftPooling.lean`, `U9DriftPower.lean`, `U9DriftPaired.lean`,
`U9DriftLocalDensity.lean`, `U9DriftClusterVariance.lean`,
`U9DriftLocalIndependence.lean`, `U9DriftDegenerateBootstrap.lean`,
`U9DriftStratification.lean` and `U9DriftBootstrapVariance.lean`. What survived, what failed, and what to attack next.

## What survived

1. **The reporting scheme is sound and the `H0` branch is the right one.** Every reported
   interval covers `1`; the replication's deliverable `0.081` really does tighten the
   pilot's `0.137`, and both of its components (precision and drift) improve
   (`replication_is_more_precise`, `replication_is_less_drifted`).
2. **Pooling does not resurrect the drift.** The inverse-variance pooled interval still
   covers `1`, with upper edge `< 1.0022` (`joint_interval_covers_one`).
3. **The "10–30×" power ask is arithmetically correct.** Under the `√m` law calibrated by
   the run itself, `10×` provably cannot resolve a 1 % deviation and `30×` provably can;
   the exact threshold is `2656` clusters.
4. **Direction stability is worth less than it looks.** `k` agreeing split-halves have null
   probability `2^{1-k}`; four of them are `1/8`, not evidence.
5. **There is a structural reason for both the null and the heavy tails.** At each odd
   prime the candidate density is `2/p` or `0` against the control's `1/p` — a `±100 %`
   local deviation — but averaged over the two quadratic classes it is *exactly* `1/p`.
   The multiplicative bias `∏(1 + χ_p(N))` has mean `1` and second moment `2^k`.
6. **The local model is not a heuristic.** The congruence conditions at distinct primes are
   *exactly* independent by the Chinese remainder theorem
   (`local_independence`, `local_independence_prod`, `missDensity_mul`); the only heuristic step left in the
   Dickman-style argument is the passage from a finite prime set to full smoothness.
7. **Cluster inference is forced, not stylistic.** The balanced two-level dispersion splits
   exactly as `total = within + between` (`anova_decomposition`), so the between-cluster
   variance is a floor that no amount of within-cluster sampling can lower
   (`pairs_cannot_beat_clusters`).

## What failed, and why

* **"√2-tightened".** False as stated: `√2` is the *ceiling* of the pooling gain and is
  attained only at matched precisions (`min_div_sqrt_two_lt_pooledHalfWidth`). Here the
  pilot is `1.93×` noisier, and the realised gain over the replication alone is under
  `12 %` (`pooling_gain_is_small`). This is a *needs-a-different-statement* failure, not a
  false conjecture: the correct statement is the ceiling theorem.
* **"Joint point ≈ 0.97".** That is the equal-weight average; the precision-weighted point
  is `≈ 0.981`. The residual tension is smaller than banked, in the direction of `H0`.
* **The quoted candidate-rate bracket.** Inward-rounded, hence not an enclosure. Fixed by
  the outward-rounded bracket.

## Bold, testable conjectures for the next cycle

### C1. Quadratic-class conditioning collapses the drift
**The key insight is** that the candidate pool is not a random pool with a small bias: at
every prime it is either doubly enriched or completely excluded, so the ratio at a *fixed*
`N` is a product of `±100 %` local factors, and only the population average is near one.
**Why now?** `U9Drift.two_class_average` and `variance_signProd` make the mean/variance
split exact, so the conditional experiment is now specified rather than heuristic:
stratify the 128 moduli by `∑_{p ≤ 100} χ_p(N)` and re-estimate. If the drift is an
artifact of an unlucky quadratic-class draw, the stratified estimator's spread should fall
by the predicted factor and the point should move to `1`.

### C2. The Dickman-approach zone has a `1 + c·log log v / log v` correction, not a constant drift
**The key insight is** that the finite-`x` correction to `ρ(u)` is logarithmic, so any
"constant −5 %" drift must in fact vary systematically with `u` across bands.
**Why now?** The catalog already contains `Shared/DickmanFiniteCorrection.lean`
(`finiteCorrection_antitoneOn`, `finiteCorrection_window`); combining it with the
band-indexed measurements turns the drift question into a *slope* question, which is far
better powered than a single-band ratio at fixed precision.

### C3. Cluster-count, not pair-count, is the only power lever
**The key insight is** that the between-`N` variance is exponentially large in the number
of small primes, so within-cluster resampling is inconsistent and adding pairs per `N`
buys nothing beyond a point.
**Why now?** `variance_signProd` gives the exact `2^k − 1`; the follow-up run can be
designed by choosing `m` from `clusterHalfWidth_lt_iff` rather than by wall-clock budget.

### C4. Paired matching is worth exactly the joint smooth rate above independence
**The key insight is** that the contrast variance is `Var X + Var Y − 2 Cov`, and for
indicators `Cov = r − pq` with `r` the joint rate, so the value of the pairing is a
*measurable* quantity that the run never reported.
**Why now?** `U9Drift.evar_sub_indicator` makes the audit a one-line computation from counts that
the patched writer now persists; if `r ≈ pq` the matching is decorative and the design can
be simplified.

### C5. Sign-stability requires depth six
**The key insight is** that a sign test over split-halves is a binomial with `2^{1-k}`, so
banking a direction-stable observation is only defensible from six splits upward.
**Why now?** `split_halves_needed_for_significance` fixes the threshold; the protocol can
adopt `k ≥ 6` as a pre-registered gate at no extra compute.

## Three concrete sub-conjectures for the next cycle

* **A (stratified null).** With the moduli stratified by `∑_{p ≤ 100} χ_p(N)`, the
  stratum-wise ratio estimator has cluster-bootstrap half width smaller than the pooled one
  by a factor predicted from `variance_signProd`; the stratified point estimate is within
  `0.01` of `1`.
* **B (finite-prime-set exactness).** *The formal half of this is now closed*:
  `local_independence_prod` gives the exact product formula for the survivor count modulo
  `∏_{p ∈ S} p`, for any finite pairwise coprime `S`, and `missDensity_eq_one_sub` turns
  each factor into `1 - (1 + χ_p(N))/p`. What remains is the measurement: compare the
  observed smooth rate at band 9 with this exact local factor and study the *residual*,
  which isolates the genuinely non-local part of any smoothness deficit.
* **C (within/between split of the realised run).** Persist per-cluster counts and evaluate
  `withinVar` and `betweenVar` of the realised `128 × 150000` design; conjecture
  `betweenVar ≥ 0.8 · totalVar`, which would show the run is already fully in the
  cluster-limited regime and that the `10–30×` follow-up must buy moduli.

## Cycle-2 addendum — the smoke-leg `NaN` is now a theorem, not an anecdote

Re-running the loop on the surviving ledger catches closed one more open item.  The ledger
attributes the smoke-leg `NaN` verdict to a "starved-regime bootstrap" (fewer than 100 of the
2000 resamples non-degenerate).  `Catalog/Probability/U9DriftDegenerateBootstrap.lean` proves
that this diagnosis is forced rather than plausible:

* `U9Drift.card_event_free_resamples` counts exactly `(m - h)^m` of the `m^m` cluster
  resamples as event-free, so the degenerate fraction is exactly `(1 - h/m)^m`
  (`U9Drift.degenerateFrac_eq`).
* `U9Drift.degenerateFrac_le_exp` gives the cluster-count-free bound `(1 - h/m)^m ≤ exp(-h)`.
* Hence `U9Drift.nondegenerate_fraction_ge`: **one** event-carrying cluster already forces at
  least a `0.632` fraction of non-degenerate resamples, for every `m`.
* Therefore `U9Drift.starved_nan_requires_event_free_population`: the observed starvation is
  incompatible with `h ≥ 1`, so the smoke leg's population carried *no* smooth hit at all.

Consequence for the protocol: a starved bootstrap should be reported as an empty event set
(no interval exists) rather than as an interval with `NaN` endpoints whose `excludes_1` field
is vacuously `True`.  This is a stronger statement than the ledger's "non-canonical" ruling —
the smoke-leg interval is not merely uninformative, it is undefined.

## Cycle-3 addendum — sub-conjecture A (quadratic-class stratification) is now closed

Running the loop once more on the surviving open items settles the *structural* half of
conjecture **C1** / sub-conjecture **A**.  `Catalog/Probability/U9DriftStratification.lean`
formalises stratified variance accounting for an arbitrary finite population and applies it
to the multiplicative-bias model of `U9DriftLocalDensity.lean`:

* `U9Drift.strat_ss_decomposition` — the exact one-way ANOVA identity
  `totalSS = withinSS + betweenSS` for *any* stratifying map, with no balance and no
  nonemptiness assumption (empty strata contribute `0` to both terms).  This is strictly
  more general than the balanced two-level identity of `U9DriftClusterVariance.lean`.
* `U9Drift.withinSS_le_totalSS` — stratification can never increase the unexplained
  dispersion, so the proposed re-analysis is safe by construction.
* `U9Drift.signProd_eq_classCount_fun` — the per-modulus bias `∏ (1 + χ_p(N))` is *exactly*
  a function of the quadratic-class count `#{p : χ_p(N) = +1}`: it equals `2 ^ k` when the
  count is `k` and `0` otherwise.  The class-count statistic proposed in sub-conjecture A is
  therefore a sufficient statistic for the bias, not merely a correlate of it.
* `U9Drift.classCount_stratification_is_exact` — hence the class-count stratification leaves
  **zero** within-stratum dispersion and explains the entire population sum of squares
  `2 ^ k (2 ^ k − 1)`, the unnormalised form of `variance_signProd`.
* `U9Drift.classCount_stratification_beats_coarse` — and the accounting is not vacuous: the
  trivial single-stratum design explains nothing, and for `k ≥ 1` the unexplained amount is
  strictly positive.

What this does *not* settle, and what the next cycle should measure: the model above treats
the bias as a product over a fixed finite prime set, so the theorem says the local part of
the between-modulus variance is entirely a class-count effect.  The empirical claim of
sub-conjecture A — that the stratified point estimate sits within `0.01` of `1` — needs the
run to persist per-cluster counts together with the class-count key; the Lean identities then
convert those counts into a decision without further modelling.  Sub-conjecture A is
accordingly split into A-structural (closed here) and A-empirical (open, cheap: it is a
re-analysis of an existing population, not a new run).

## Cycle-4 addendum — sub-conjecture C3 (cluster count is the only power lever) is now closed exactly

One more turn of the loop settles the structural half of conjecture **C3**.
`Catalog/Probability/U9DriftBootstrapVariance.lean` models the cluster bootstrap exactly:
its resample space is the finite set of all `m ^ m` index maps `s : Fin m → Fin m`, each
equally likely, and the resampled statistic is the mean of the resampled cluster values.

* `U9Drift.sum_resample_prod` — the marginalisation identity `∑_s ∏_i F i (s i) = ∏_i ∑_j F i j`.
  This is the *exact finite-sample* form of the statement "the resample coordinates are
  independent"; it is proved from `Finset.prod_univ_sum`, not assumed.
* `U9Drift.sum_resample_eval` / `U9Drift.sum_resample_eval_pair` — its one- and
  two-coordinate corollaries `m^(m-1) ∑ g` and `m^(m-2) (∑ g)(∑ h)`.  The second is what
  kills the cross terms, because the recentred cluster values sum to zero.
* `U9Drift.bootVar_eq` — **the exact bootstrap variance law**: over the full resample space
  the variance of the resample mean is exactly `evar c / m`.  The `1/m` (hence the `√m`
  law used in `U9DriftPower.lean` to pin the follow-up at `2656` clusters) is an identity
  at every `m`, not a large-`m` approximation.
* `U9Drift.cluster_bootVar_eq` — applied to the realised balanced design, the cluster
  bootstrap variance is exactly `betweenVar x / m`.  The within-cluster dispersion does not
  appear at all: the `150000` pairs per modulus enter only through the *value* of
  `betweenVar`, never through the `1/m` rate.  With `U9Drift.bootVar_le_totalVar_div` and
  `U9Drift.clusters_needed_iff` this becomes the design rule in usable form — a target
  standard error `t` needs `m ≥ evar c / t²` clusters, whatever the pair count.
* `U9Drift.bootVar_pos_of_ne` / `U9Drift.bootVar_eq_zero_of_const` — the accounting is
  sharp and non-vacuous: the bootstrap spread vanishes exactly for a constant cluster
  population, so two differing moduli already force a strictly positive interval.

What remains open in C3 is only the empirical half: the *value* of `betweenVar` for the
realised `128 × 150000` design (sub-conjecture **C**), which needs per-cluster counts to be
persisted.  The Lean identities then convert those counts directly into the cluster count

A fourth cycle adds an exact model of the cluster bootstrap on its full m^m resample space: a marginalisation identity that is the finite-sample form of resample-coordinate independence, and from it the exact law that the bootstrap variance of the resample mean equals the population variance divided by m, hence exactly betweenVar/m for the realised two-level design, with no within-cluster term at all."
